correctness.rationale: Independently reconstructed each digit-length contribution and the error identity. For every b>=2, k>=4 bounds follow directly from two fixed initial digits; a geometric bound handles all k>=8. The 3-digit deficit differs from H_b by less than 2 on b^3 scaling, using an exact telescope and a bounded elementary denominator correction. Their signed interval sum has absolute size at most 4. The separate exact Fraction checker confirms b=2..6, k=1..7 without treating finite tests as a proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The full 2019 published paper treats the same object and all bases, but with weaker remainder bounds; the 1981 result treats all fixed bases for convergence only. Later digit-counting and base-comparison sources concern different observables and do not imply the sharp coefficient.

originality.rationale: The 1981 primary solution concerns fixed-base convergence; 2019 JIS Theorem 4 provides only an O(log b/b^3) estimate plus a positive limsup, and Theorem 5 merely reformulates the main term. The new result proves a normalized limit equal to one and a uniformly bounded arithmetic-centered remainder; these do not follow from the cited bounds alone. Actual semantic and bibliographic searches found no directly covering result; residual unindexed equivalence risk is disclosed.
residual_risks: The preprint full text was not independently exhaustively read; its later open-access journal incarnation was inspected fully.
Unindexed sources or equivalent alternative normalizations could duplicate the sharpened limit; search failure alone does not prove priority.

value.rationale: A previously identified sharp logarithmic error scale had no known leading coefficient or proven normalized convergence. Determining exactly 1 and a uniform bounded recentered remainder is a natural analytic invariant of the historical reciprocal-palindrome question, with substantive asymptotic information unavailable from the original Omega-plus / O-star estimates.
